Issued at 236 PM EDT Tue Aug 18 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Disheveled longwave troughing over northeastern North America to be 
the primary influence of the region over the forecast period, with 
occasional shortwave trough passages to move through the region, 
most of which will be maturing / closed off, and may have some 
hangtime across the Great Lakes owing to standard stagnant August 
jet dynamics. 

Currently, a mature upper low over Hudson Bay to continue an 
eastward trek, with antecedent SW return flow drawing in warmer and 
(to an extent) more moist air across the Great Lakes. Surface 
dewpoints have already ballooned to the 60 to 66 range across the 
region as of the noon hour, with evidence of prefrontal clearing 
building into northern Michigan. Surface cold frontal boundary 
roughly stretching from James Bay through Marquette and WSW through 
Minnesota just north of the Twin Cities. Evidence of some mixing 
trying to manifest just ahead of this cold frontal boundary... which 
may be something to watch for across our neck of the woods. 
Nonetheless, frontal boundary to pass through the region with just 
enough instability to force a convective response across Wisconsin, 
eventually leaking into northern lower late this afternoon into the 
evening, with showers and storms gradually clearing through the 
evening / night from WNW to ESE. 

Surface high pressure to build on the backside of the front, 
yielding an aggressive drying NW wind regime (in conjunction with 
500mb height rises / shortwave ridging) through the day Wednesday 
that will bring back sunnier skies and seasonable warmth during the 
day and again Thursday... but with the dry nature of the airmass and 
calming winds overnight, cooler nights to return Wednesday and 
Thursday nights. Next wave digs from the NNW starting Friday, with 
current trend pointing to this wave occluding / closing off overhead 
through the course of the weekend, bringing back cooler and 
unsettled conditions for at least the start of the weekend (and 
perhaps a renewed severe threat Friday?). High pressure / 500mb 
shortwave ridging to follow through the day Sunday and into Monday 
before the next wave passes through at the end of the forecast 
period.

Details: 

Shower / Storm Potential This Afternoon / Tonight: Aforementioned 
frontal boundary to traverse the region this evening into tonight, 
which looks to suffice in the forcing department (albeit, to a 
limited extent... as pointed out by previous forecaster, frontal 
convergence leaves a bit to be desired). Latest CAMs seem bound and 
determined to have an aggressive prefrontal mixing regime, 
particularly across northeast lower with downsloping WSW winds. Will 
have to see how aggressive this trends as it will be pivotal to the 
generation of this evening's instability, and thus the evolution of 
any convection. Nonetheless, the other thing CAMs are persistent 
with is deeper moisture right along / ahead of the front pooling 
across the region, and thus giving us instability in the order of 
500 to 800 J/kg of MLCAPE. Several fascinating aspects to this setup 
to unpack... first and foremost, most modeled soundings showcase a 
pseudo-inverted-V profile that usually comes with gustier storms 
that don't really produce much in the way of rainfall... but with 
largely unidirectional flow, anticipate it is possible if (and it's 
a BIG ole "if") we can maintain instability following any intial 
convection, which could support increasingly heavier rainfall in any 
additional storm formation. A majority of CAMs seem to find this 
idea possible, but I admittedly have my doubts.

Aforementioned unidirectional flow will be a big player in any 
potential convective evolution. Hodograph shape this evening will 
largely be linear, and as such, while this does eventually favor an 
outflow dominant multicellular / linear mode... should be noted that 
upon convective initiation (when storms are most discrete), this does 
favor splitting cells... with potential for an initial left mover 
dominant regime before transitioning into a linear mode with time... 
and select CAMs have this down to a tee across the NW lower 
shoreline, perhaps scraping the very southern reaches of Mackinac 
County... As such, there is potential for an intial hail dominant 
severe threat across the aforementioned regions before transitioning 
to a linear, more wind / outflow dominant mode this evening. Should 
note... we probably only achieve the most marginal of severe 
conditions at best if we can hold onto progged instability trends... 
but in the event we trend more downward with instability, the threat 
may become much more muted. Nonetheless, enough is there for SPC to 
expand the inherited Day 1 Marginal Risk (1/5) across all of 
northern lower, butting up right against eastern upper. Primary
